title: Water Quality and Conservation
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Water Quality and Conservation Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Assess the effects of human activities on the quality and quantity of water; describe how water is treated and how communities, including First Nations, work to protect water; evaluate ways to conserve water. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand E: Earth and Space Systems – Water Systems)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 science worksheets on water pollution, drinking water treatment, Walkerton, boil-water advisories, water walks and conserving water. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Runoff and waste pollute water; treatment, wetlands and conservation keep it safe.
body_html:
How to think about it

Human activities affect the quality and amount of water.

  • Point sources (a pipe) and non-point sources (lawns, roads, farms) pollute water.
  • Water treatment plants make water safe to drink; wastewater plants clean used water.
  • Conserve water: fix leaks, take shorter showers, plant native gardens, use less salt and fertilizer.
Example

What kind of source is runoff from many farms?

spread over a large area

Answer: non-point source

Example

Why do mayfly larvae show a healthy stream?

they need clean, oxygen-rich water

Answer: they are indicator species

Common mistakes

  • Thinking water is unlimited because it falls as rain.
  • Thinking storm drains go to treatment plants.
  • Thinking clear water is always safe to drink.

faq.q: How is drinking water made safe?
faq.a: It is settled, filtered and disinfected (usually with chlorine) at a treatment plant, and tested often.

faq.q: Why are there boil-water advisories in some First Nations communities?
faq.a: Some communities do not have reliable water treatment, so water must be boiled to be safe. Governments and communities are working to fix this.
Turn off the tap while brushing, take shorter showers, report leaks and keep pollution out of storm drains.

items.q: What is frost wedging?
c: Water freezes in cracks, expands and breaks rock apart.
items.e: Physical weathering.

items.q: What is permeability?
c: how easily water can flow through a material
items.e: Connected pores.

items.q: What is a low-flow showerhead?
c: a showerhead that uses less water per minute
items.e: It saves water and the energy to heat it.

items.q: Which water property lets it dissolve so many minerals?
items.e: Universal solvent.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by burning garbage in the open?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the air.

items.q: Noah's class studies this problem: “Forests are cleared for new houses.” Which solution would best reduce the impact?
c: keeping protected green spaces and wildlife corridors
planting grass buffer strips along the river and using less fertilizer
cooling the water in ponds before it is released
public transit, electric vehicles and cleaner power
items.e: A good solution targets the cause of the impact.

items.q: How does climate change affect Ontario's water systems?
c: It has no effect on water.
It changes rain and snow patterns, causing more floods and droughts and warmer lakes.
It makes all lakes freeze longer.
items.e: Warmer lakes can grow more harmful algae.

items.q: Leah observes: “Plastic bags blow into the ocean.” What impact can this have?
c: algae blooms that use up oxygen and kill fish
animals swallowing or getting tangled in plastic
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by smoke from factory chimneys?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the air.

items.q: What is a conservation authority in Ontario?
c: an agency that manages and protects a watershed
items.e: Ontario has 36 conservation authorities.

items.q: What happens to water's volume when it freezes?
items.e: Ice is less dense.

items.q: Ethan's class studies this problem: “Fertilizer runs off farms into a river.” Which solution would best reduce the impact?
c: reusable bags and bans on single-use plastic
rain gardens and permeable sidewalk that soak up runoff
cooling the water in ponds before it is released
planting grass buffer strips along the river and using less fertilizer
items.e: A good solution targets the cause of the impact.

items.q: How does road salt affect water systems?
c: It washes into streams and groundwater and can harm plants and animals.
It only stays on the road.
items.e: Use only as much salt as needed.

items.q: Why do many First Nations communities in Canada have boil-water advisories?
c: Their water systems do not always provide safe drinking water.
items.e: Safe water is a human right that Canada is working to provide.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by oil spilled from a ship?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the water.

items.q: What is a harmful algal bloom?
c: a fast growth of algae that can make water unsafe and lower oxygen
a flower show by a lake
items.e: Lake Erie has had large blooms.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by smoke from a ship's engine at sea?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the air.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by old batteries thrown into the soil?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the land.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by honking horns in heavy traffic?
items.e: Loud sounds disturb people and animals.

items.q: Why should you never pour paint or oil down a storm drain?
c: It makes the drain work better.
Storm drains usually flow straight to rivers and lakes without treatment.
items.e: Many drains are marked 'Drains to the lake.'

items.q: Which of these causes air pollution?
c: paint washed into a monsoon drain
items.e: Smoke from factory chimneys leads to air pollution.

items.q: Does water disappear when a puddle dries up?
c: No. It evaporates into the air as water vapour.
items.e: The water is still in the air.

items.q: Why does a cold drink can get wet on the outside?
c: Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold surface.
items.e: Condensation.

items.q: What is water vapour?
items.e: We cannot see water vapour.

items.q: What is water vapour?
items.e: We cannot see it.

items.q: What are clouds made of?
c: tiny droplets of water (or ice crystals)
items.e: Vapour condenses into droplets.

items.q: What is a point source of pollution?
c: pollution from a whole city's roads
pollution from one clear place, like a factory pipe
items.e: Non-point sources come from many places.

items.q: What is non-point source pollution?
c: pollution from many spread-out places, like lawns and roads
items.e: It is harder to control.

items.q: Why should old medicines be returned to a pharmacy instead of flushed?
c: Treatment plants cannot remove all medicines, so they end up in lakes.
items.e: Take-back programs protect water.

items.q: Why do towns have water restrictions during a drought?
c: There is little rain, so the stored water must last longer.
items.e: Saving water helps everyone.

items.q: Which part of the water cycle happens when a puddle dries up?
items.e: Liquid to gas.

items.q: What powers the water cycle?
items.e: The Sun evaporates water.

items.q: Does the water cycle make new water?
c: No. The same water moves round and round.
items.e: The water on Earth is reused.

items.q: Where is most of Earth's water?
items.e: About 97% of Earth's water is salty sea water.

items.q: What happened in Walkerton, Ontario, in 2000?
c: E. coli bacteria got into the town's drinking water and many people became sick.
A drought dried up all wells.
items.e: It led to stronger water safety laws in Ontario.

items.q: What does a water treatment plant do?
c: removes particles and germs to make water safe to drink
items.e: Steps include filtering and disinfecting.

items.q: Which of these causes land pollution?
c: old batteries thrown into the soil
chemicals from a factory poured into a river
items.e: Old batteries thrown into the soil leads to land pollution.

items.q: Which uses the most water in a typical Canadian home?
items.e: Low-flow fixtures save water.

items.q: Which of these causes water pollution?
c: paint washed into a monsoon drain
loud music played near a nature reserve
items.e: Paint washed into a monsoon drain leads to water pollution.

items.q: Why does warm water hold less life in a lake?
c: Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen.
items.e: Thermal pollution lowers oxygen.

items.q: Which of these wastes water?
c: using a pail instead of a hose to wash the car
thawing frozen food under a running tap
watering plants with water used to wash rice
items.e: Water is precious; every drop counts.

items.q: Which of these is a way to save water?
c: taking a long bath every day
thawing frozen food under a running tap
turning off the tap while brushing teeth
items.e: Saving water means using only what we need.

items.q: Which household product is safest for the water system?
c: a drain cleaner poured down the sink every day
motor oil poured on the driveway
old medicine flushed down the toilet
items.e: Choose products that break down safely.

items.q: What does pH measure in water?
c: how acidic or basic the water is
items.e: Most aquatic life needs a pH near 7.

items.q: Which of these wastes water?
c: watering plants with water used to wash rice
washing a few clothes in a full machine
using a pail instead of a hose to wash the car
turning off the tap while brushing teeth
items.e: Water is precious; every drop counts.

items.q: What is a rain garden?
c: a planted dip that soaks up runoff from roofs and driveways
a garden that only grows in rain
items.e: Rain gardens reduce flooding and pollution.

using a pail instead of a hose to wash the car

items.q: Why is it best to water lawns in the early morning?
c: Water is cleaner in the morning.
Less water evaporates before it soaks in.
items.e: Smart watering conserves water.

items.q: Which indicator suggests a stream is healthy?
c: many mayfly and stonefly larvae living in it
lots of foam and a bad smell
items.e: Some insects need clean water.

items.q: Which is a source of water pollution?
c: fertilizer and manure washing off farm fields
items.e: Runoff carries nutrients and chemicals.

items.q:

Mondaycold, still and cloudy9
Thursdaycool and windy6
Wednesdaywarm, sunny and windy3
Kai timed how long the same wet T-shirt took to dry on the washing line. On which day did the T-shirt dry fastest?
items.e: Warm, sunny and windy weather speeds up evaporation.

items.q: Iron in rocks reacts with water and oxygen and turns red-brown. Which type of weathering is this?
items.e: Physical weathering breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering changes the minerals.

items.q: A glass of water is left on a sunny windowsill for a week. The water level drops. Where has the water gone?
c: It has soaked into the glass.
It has evaporated into the air as water vapour.
items.e: The water will become part of the water cycle.

items.q: How can water pollution harm living things?
c: Fish and other water animals may die.
items.e: Polluted water may have harmful substances.

items.q: In a model of the water cycle, a bowl of hot water is covered with plastic wrap and ice is put on top. What does the ice do?
c: It cools the plastic wrap so water vapour condenses on it.
items.e: The cold film is like the cool air high up.

items.q: Why does a plastic sheet placed over a hole in the sand collect water on its underside on a sunny day?
c: Water evaporates from the sand and condenses on the cooler sheet.
items.e: This is a model of the water cycle.

items.q: In the same model, what do the drops falling back into the bowl represent?
items.e: Water droplets join and fall back.

items.q: Waves hurl sand against a cliff and wear it away. Which type of weathering is this?
items.e: Physical weathering breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering changes the minerals.

items.q: What does a wastewater treatment plant do?
c: cleans used water from homes before it returns to lakes and rivers
makes drinking water from the ocean
items.e: Sewage must be treated.

items.q: Which test result suggests water has a lot of pollution from fertilizer?
c: high levels of nitrates and phosphates
items.e: Nutrients feed algae blooms.

items.q: Why do living things need water?
c: Water is needed only for washing.
All living things need water to survive and carry out life processes.
items.e: Water is needed for digestion, transport and photosynthesis.

items.q: Pebbles in a river knock together and become rounded. Which type of weathering is this?
items.e: Physical weathering breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering changes the minerals.

items.q: What is NEWater?
c: used water that is treated to make it clean enough to reuse
items.e: It is cleaned using advanced membranes and ultraviolet light.

items.q: Rainwater with CO₂ dissolves a marble statue. Which type of weathering is this?
items.e: Physical weathering breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering changes the minerals.

items.q: What is desalination?
c: removing salt from seawater to make fresh water
items.e: It uses a lot of energy.

items.q: Why do some industries reuse cooling water?
c: to save water and reduce thermal pollution
to make water hotter for rivers
items.e: Recycling water saves resources.

items.q: Which of these causes water pollution?
items.e: Drains lead to canals and reservoirs.

items.q: Why is it important to keep reservoirs clean?
c: Reservoir water is treated and used as drinking water.
items.e: Pollution makes water harder and more costly to treat.

items.q: Why are wetlands important to water systems?
c: They filter pollutants, store floodwater and recharge groundwater.
items.e: Protecting wetlands protects water.

items.q: Ice forms in a crack and splits a boulder. Which type of weathering is this?
items.e: Physical weathering breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering changes the minerals.

items.q: Feldspar in granite slowly changes into clay in wet soil. Which type of weathering is this?
items.e: Physical weathering breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering changes the minerals.

items.q: Why does water in a wide plate evaporate faster than in a narrow cup?
c: More of the water's surface is open to the air.
items.e: Surface area.

items.q: Mei covers a bowl of salty water with cling wrap and puts a small cup in the middle. After a day in the sun, fresh water is in the cup. Which processes happened?
items.e: This is how a solar still works.

items.q: A shower uses about 9 litres of water a minute. How much water is saved by cutting a shower from 10 minutes to 5 minutes?
items.e: 5 minutes × 9 litres = 45 litres.

items.q: Why does washing dry faster on a windy day?
c: Wind is cold, so it dries faster.
Wind carries water vapour away, so more water can evaporate.
items.e: Moving air speeds evaporation.

items.q: Lucas's family used 600 litres of water in a week. They cut their use by 120 litres the next week. How much did they use the next week?
Why is it important to have clean rivers, even though water is recycled?
c: Rivers are not part of the water cycle.
Pollution can stay in the water as it moves through the cycle.
items.e: Protect water.

items.q: Why do Indigenous water walkers walk around the Great Lakes?
c: to honour water as sacred and raise awareness about protecting it
items.e: Josephine Mandamin led many water walks.

items.q: Why do the windows of a warm kitchen steam up in winter?
c: Water vapour from cooking condenses on the cold glass.
items.e: Warm vapour meets cold glass.

items.q: How could you show that evaporation depends on temperature?
c: Put the same amount of water in identical dishes in warm and cold places and measure what is left.
Put them all in one place.
items.e: Fair test.

items.q: Water droplets formed on the inside of the cover. What processes took place?
items.e: Water evaporated and condensed on the cooler cover.

items.q: A pupil left identical bowls of water in an open field and under a shelter. The water in the open field evaporated faster. Which factor most likely caused this?
c: more sunlight and wind in the open field
items.e: Temperature and wind speed up evaporation.

items.q: Why do deltas form where rivers enter the ocean?
c: The river slows down and drops the sediment it was carrying.
items.e: Deposition.

items.q: Hana put 200 mL of water in a covered and an uncovered beaker in the same sunny place. After a week, which had more water left?
items.e: The cover stopped the water vapour from escaping.

items.q: Design an investigation: does freezing break rock? What is a good plan?
c: Heat rocks in an oven only.
Soak identical rock samples, freeze and thaw some many times, keep others at room temperature, and compare cracks.
Freeze one rock once and look.
items.e: Control and repetition.

items.q: A farmer's field floods easily and water stays on top. Which soil is likely?
c: clay, because it has low permeability
items.e: Drainage.

items.q: Chloe wants to find out whether wind makes washing dry faster. Which is the fairest test?
c: two identical wet towels, one in front of a fan and one without
one wet towel and one dry towel
two towels in different rooms with different heaters
items.e: Only the wind should change.

items.q: Why does a toilet mirror fog up after a hot shower?
c: Water vapour condenses on the cool mirror.
items.e: Warm, moist air cools on the glass.

items.q: A gravestone made of marble is harder to read than one made of granite of the same age. Why?
c: Marble dissolves more easily in slightly acidic rain.
items.e: Chemical weathering rate.

items.q: Which action conserves water at home?
c: washing a car with a running hose
fixing leaky taps and taking shorter showers
running the tap while brushing teeth
items.e: Small changes save a lot of water.

items.q: Why are potholes worse after winters with many freeze–thaw cycles?
c: Each cycle of freezing water widens cracks in the road.
items.e: Frost wedging.
